record.tranche_reason: The study measures how SAE features correspond across dictionary sizes and finds both similar/split features and features with no close match. This refines the idea that dictionary features are stable, canonical units, but it does not directly test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The reported feature comparisons, reconstruction effects, and feature swaps bear on SAE feature representations and their stability across dictionary sizes. The Frankenstein SAE performance comparisons are results of the authors' proposed construction, not direct tests of the listed claim versions, so they are not rows. The 0.7 similarity threshold is described as an arbitrary choice and is not itself a result row.
record.test_reason: The study compares SAE features on the same GPT-2 site across dictionary widths. About 35% of the larger SAE's features carry information absent from the smaller SAE, and many others are split or redundant versions of its features. This bears on whether SAE features are complete, stable units (V5). It uses SAEs as a tool rather than testing whether LLMs contain sparse features (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that scaling up an SAE yields novel features (information absent from the smaller SAE) and reconstruction features (split or sparser versions of existing ones). Novel features can be added and reconstruction features swapped, enabling stitched Frankenstein SAEs with lower MSE but higher L0. They call the metric and threshold somewhat arbitrary and generality uncertain.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares decoder-direction similarities and reconstruction effects across SAE dictionary sizes; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition setup or its measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The feature categorization depends on decoder cosine similarity and the chosen 0.7 threshold; the authors call both the metric choice and threshold somewhat arbitrary.
record.problems: The authors describe the decoder-cosine metric and 0.7 cutoff as somewhat arbitrary. Generalization beyond the tested residual-stream SAEs is unclear; only two Pythia SAEs are mentioned as similar results, and MLP/attention layers and much larger models were not tested. Several results are qualitative or presented in figures without numerical values. The study does not evaluate the features on specific tasks.
record.rows_left_out: No other results meeting the row criteria were omitted. Frankenstein-versus-standard-SAE reconstruction performance and L0 comparisons are excluded because they evaluate the authors' proposed stitched method rather than directly testing the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition, or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or feature-importance allocation.
SAEs are used as given; the study does not test whether features are spread across neurons or whether sparse features are recovered.
Not tested: stability across seeds, layers other than GPT-2 L8 and Pythia L3, MLP/attention sites, larger models, or task-level validity.
Whether features are one-dimensional is not tested; the weekday-splitting geometry appears only in comments.

missing.what: Feature-family (splitting) graphs between GPT2-768 and GPT2-1536, and the interpolation from GPT-768 to GPT-12288 across larger SAE pairs. These show parent/child splitting structure relevant to how canonical features are.
missing.locator: Can we swap features between SAEs? (family-structure figure; transition figure)

missing.what: Boxplots of MSE change for additions across larger SAE pairs beyond 768/1536, showing the same novel/reconstruction split.
missing.locator: Can we add features from one SAE to another? (boxplot figure)

record.verdict_notes: V4 links were removed from all rows. The study assumes that SAEs recover features and does not test it, so the record's V4 supports label is dropped. The record's V5 supports label rested partly on r13, which concerns the authors' own method. Comments (weekday splitting, a heptagon layout) are not study results.

versions.untested_parts: No small toy networks or toy-model superposition geometry are tested.
The study does not measure neuron polysemanticity, feature importance, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The study does not investigate causes of polysemantic neurons other than capacity pressure.
Tests SAE feature dictionaries on GPT-2 and Pythia residual streams; does not establish that the extracted features are ground-truth features or measure how many neurons each feature spans.
Tests feature correspondence across SAE widths and decoder finetuning, not completeness or canonicality across architectures, layers, training runs, or tasks.
Decoder directions are compared as vectors, but the study does not test whether model features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small layer 8 resid_pre, GPT2-768 vs GPT2-1536
relationships.reason: Smaller dictionaries miss about 35% of the larger SAE's information-bearing features. Adding those features cuts MSE by almost 10% (r1, r3, r5, r6, r7, r9), so a given-width SAE is not a complete feature set.
relationships.display_finding: The 768-latent SAE lacked about 35% of the 1536-latent SAE's information-bearing features, and adding them cut reconstruction MSE by almost 10%, so an SAE of any one width is not a complete feature set.

relationships.condition: Features shared across widths (cosine >0.7), GPT-2 and Pythia
relationships.reason: Shared features persist across widths (r2) but appear as split or redundant variants: adding them mostly raises MSE (r8), and swaps trade MSE for L0 (r10, r11). Pythia is reported as similar without numbers (r12).
relationships.display_finding: Shared features persisted across widths but as split or redundant variants: adding them mostly raised MSE and swapping them traded MSE for L0, with Pythia reported as similar.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 layer 8 resid_pre; Pythia-410M-deduped layer 3 resid_pre
reader_labels.reason: The study trains and compares sparse SAE dictionaries on language-model activations and reports features that reconstruct information, including features with no close match at the smaller width (r1, r3, r6, r12). It does not establish ground-truth feature recovery.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Features with close cross-width matches and Frankenstein decoder finetuning
reader_labels.reason: Many larger-SAE features are reported as similar to smaller-SAE features, and most Frankenstein decoder directions remain highly similar to their base counterparts (r1, r2, r13).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 layer 8 resid_pre, especially features classified as novel at the wider SAE size
reader_labels.reason: A substantial group is reported as novel or without a close smaller-SAE counterpart; adding low-similarity features improves reconstruction, while adding many high-similarity features tends to worsen it (r1, r3, r7, r8, r9). This is evidence against treating every SAE dictionary as a complete, size-independent canonical feature set.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Replacing parent features with related larger-SAE features usually reduces L0 but most swaps increase MSE, so correspondence across widths does not imply interchangeable features without a reconstruction trade-off (r10, r11).
